candidates.title: Training with Quantization Noise for Extreme Model Compression
candidates.abstract: We tackle the problem of producing compact models, maximizing their accuracy for a given model size. A standard solution is to train networks with Quantization Aware Training, where the weights are quantized during training and the gradients approximated with the Straight-Through Estimator. In this paper, we extend this approach to work beyond int8 fixed-point quantization with extreme compression methods where the approximations introduced by STE are severe, such as Product Quantization. Our proposal is to only quantize a different random subset of weights during each forward, allowing for unbiased gradients to flow through the other weights. Controlling the amount of noise and its form allows for extreme compression rates while maintaining the performance of the original model. As a result we establish new state-of-the-art compromises between accuracy and model size both in natural language processing and image classification. For example, applying our method to state-of-the-art Transformer and ConvNet architectures, we can achieve 82.5% accuracy on MNLI by compressing RoBERTa to 14MB and 80.0 top-1 accuracy on ImageNet by compressing an EfficientNet-B3 to 3.3MB.
candidates.reason: 学習方式自体はquantization-aware trainingだが、最終成果はRoBERTa/Transformerの極端な圧縮とdeployment memory削減であり、推論向けweight compressionの対象範囲に入る。RoBERTaを14MBまで圧縮しMNLI 82.5%を維持する実証を持つ。
candidates.library_body_check: fulltext_relevance_review: arXiv一次本文/abstractを確認。各forwardで異なるweight subsetだけを量子化してunbiased gradient経路を残すQuant-Noiseを提案し、int8を超えるproduct quantization等へ対応。RoBERTaを14MBまで圧縮しMNLI 82.5%、Transformer language modelでも極端圧縮を評価しており、推論時model footprint削減へ直結する。

candidates.title: Funnel-Transformer: Filtering out Sequential Redundancy for Efficient Language Processing
candidates.abstract: With the success of language pretraining, it is highly desirable to develop more efficient architectures of good scalability that can exploit the abundant unlabeled data at a lower cost. To improve the efficiency, we examine the much-overlooked redundancy in maintaining a full-length token-level presentation, especially for tasks that only require a single-vector presentation of the sequence. With this intuition, we propose Funnel-Transformer which gradually compresses the sequence of hidden states to a shorter one and hence reduces the computation cost. More importantly, by re-investing the saved FLOPs from length reduction in constructing a deeper or wider model, we further improve the model capacity. In addition, to perform token-level predictions as required by common pretraining objectives, Funnel-Transformer is able to recover a deep representation for each token from the reduced hidden sequence via a decoder. Empirically, with comparable or fewer FLOPs, Funnel-Transformer outperforms the standard Transformer on a wide variety of sequence-level prediction tasks, including text classification, language understanding, and reading comprehension. The code and pretrained checkpoints are available at this https URL.
candidates.reason: token-level hidden sequenceを層間で段階的に短縮し、後段Transformerの計算量を削減するlanguage-model architecture。sequence-level NLPで同等以下FLOPsで標準Transformerを上回り、推論時にも短い内部sequenceを使うため対象。
candidates.library_body_check: fulltext_relevance_review: arXiv一次本文/abstractを確認。full-length token representationの冗長性を問題化し、encoder内でhidden sequenceをpoolして短縮、必要なtoken-level predictionはdecoderで復元する。削減FLOPsをdepth/widthへ再投資可能で、標準Transformerよりcomparable/fewer FLOPsでclassification、NLU、reading comprehensionを改善。

candidates.title: CODI: Compressing Chain-of-Thought into Continuous Space via Self-Distillation
candidates.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
candidates.abstract: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning enhances Large Language Models (LLMs) by encouraging step-by-step reasoning in natural language. However, leveraging a latent continuous space for reasoning may offer benefits in terms of both efficiency and robustness. Prior implicit CoT methods attempt to bypass language completely by reasoning in continuous space but have consistently underperformed compared to the standard explicit CoT approach. We introduce CODI (Continuous Chain-of-Thought via Self-Distillation), a novel training framework that effectively compresses natural language CoT into continuous space. CODI jointly trains a teacher task (Explicit CoT) and a student task (Implicit CoT), distilling the reasoning ability from language into continuous space by aligning the hidden states of a designated token. Our experiments show that CODI is the first implicit CoT approach to match the performance of explicit CoT on GSM8k at the GPT-2 scale, achieving a 3.1x compression rate and outperforming the previous state-of-the-art by 28.2% in accuracy. CODI also demonstrates robustness, generalizable to complex datasets, and interpretability. These results validate that LLMs can reason effectively not only in natural language, but also in a latent continuous space. Code is available at https://github.com/zhenyi4/codi.

candidates.reason: 明示的CoTを連続潜在空間へ圧縮して推論時のreasoning token列を短縮するLLM reasoning efficiency研究。GSM8kで明示CoT性能を維持しつつ3.1x圧縮を報告し、生成token削減が推論計算へ直接効くため対象。
candidates.library_body_check: fulltext_relevance_review: arXiv一次本文/abstractを確認。teacher explicit-CoTとstudent implicit-CoTを同一modelでjoint trainingし、最終回答tokenのhidden stateをalignしてcontinuous thoughtへ蒸留。GPT-2 scaleのGSM8kでexplicit CoTに匹敵し3.1x compression、論文の効率分析では短いcontinuous thoughtにより推論生成を削減。

candidates.title: Mini-Omni: Language Models Can Hear, Talk While Thinking in Streaming
candidates.abstract: Recent advances in language models have achieved significant progress. GPT-4o, as a new milestone, has enabled real-time conversations with humans, demonstrating near-human natural fluency. Such human-computer interaction necessitates models with the capability to perform reasoning directly with the audio modality and generate output in streaming. However, this remains beyond the reach of current academic models, as they typically depend on extra TTS systems for speech synthesis, resulting in undesirable latency. This paper introduces the Mini-Omni, an audio-based end-to-end conversational model, capable of real-time speech interaction. To achieve this capability, we propose a text-instructed speech generation method, along with batch-parallel strategies during inference to further boost the performance. Our method also helps to retain the original model's language capabilities with minimal degradation, enabling other works to establish real-time interaction capabilities. We call this training method"Any Model Can Talk". We also introduce the VoiceAssistant-400K dataset to fine-tune models optimized for speech output. To our best knowledge, Mini-Omni is the first fully end-to-end, open-source model for real-time speech interaction, offering valuable potential for future research.
candidates.reason: end-to-end audio LLMのreal-time speech interactionを目的に、外部TTS依存によるlatencyを避け、推論時batch-parallel strategyでstreaming生成性能を改善する。リアルタイムLLM推論が明示的最終目的なので対象。
candidates.library_body_check: fulltext_relevance_review: arXiv一次abstractを精査。外部TTSがundesirable latencyを生むことを問題化し、audio-based end-to-end conversational LM、text-instructed speech generation、inference時batch-parallel strategyを導入してreal-time speech interactionを実現する。推論latencyが方式設計の直接動機。
